messages.subject: Commercial shiny-app
parts:
Hey, everyone! 


I'd like to create kind of online calculator and try to earn some money on advanced functionality and/or on ads. So, my idea is to create own server in cloud (perhaps, based on AWS), install R, "Shiny" library and etc (without Rstudio). Is it legal in sense of their licences?


Thx for reading and help in advence.

messages.author: edbcc711cdbb3da8
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Commercial shiny-app
parts:
Hi Stepan,
We can't provide any legal advice ourselves, but given that you aren't bundling shiny server with an offering that you are distributing you likely don't need to worry about shiny server being licensed under an AGPL license so you could run your own shiny server in the cloud (AWS, Azure, Google etc...) and/or you can also use shinyapps.io to host your running shiny applications if you so desire.     With shinyapps.io, we would be operating the service for you and you can focus on the creation of your applications.  As long as you aren't using our trademark (and it sounds like you aren't hosting the IDE), you should be good to go.  Again, we aren't lawyers and can't dispense legal advice, but hopefully that gives you a sense for what is possible.
Best,
-Tareef
